answer: Physical clock-skew fingerprinting mitigates Sybil attacks by measuring microsecond timing drifts in the quartz oscillator of an agent during network challenges. Attackers incur the verifiable hardware cost of buying distinct timing crystals instead of virtualizing infinite nodes on one machine. Whether monitoring an oasis or a juniper grove, agents cannot emulate these physical silicon flaws. However, ambient temperature shifts can distort clock drift, incorrectly rejecting honest agents.
